steps: Check the opening & chimney
Minimum opening 23-1/2" high, 33-1/2" front width, 16-3/8" deep, 24-1/2" back width. Chimney 10' to 50' tall: masonry 6" x 8" or factory-built solid fuel 7" minimum inside diameter.

Liner length

  1. Remove and discard the existing chimney cap.
  2. With one person at the fireplace opening and one at the top of the chimney, measure from the fireplace base to the top of the chimney.
  3. Subtract the height of the insert. The result is the length of co-linear flexible aluminum pipe needed; cut #816 to that length.

Placement

  • Level surface able to support the insert and venting; out of traffic, away from furniture and draperies. May be installed in a bedroom.
  • Smoke shelves, shields and baffles may be removed if attached by mechanical fasteners; remove firebrick if needed to reach the minimum opening. Cutting sheet metal parts of the existing fireplace is prohibited.
  • If the metal floor is removed, set the insert directly on the metal base of the metal fireplace.
  • Mechanically attach the 'THIS UNIT HAS BEEN MODIFIED' label at the bottom of the existing firebox, where it stays visible if the insert is removed.

Outdoor covered installation (Section 6.8)

Operation approved from 40°F to 110°F. The overhang in front, and to each side, must be at least 1/2 of the roofline elevation above the base of the fireplace. Wiring per the outdoor requirements of NECA NFPA 70; black painted safety barriers are highly recommended.
Prepare the fireplace
Verify the chimney is non-combustible and clean; block the damper fully open or remove it, and remove the chimney cap. Plan the gas line (right side) and power, and attach the conversion label.

• Verify the chimney is non-combustible, clean and in good working order; clean the chimney and fireplace to keep creosote odor out of the home.
  • Verify combustible mantel and sidewall clearances against Section 8.0 (see Clearances).
  • Refractory, glass doors, screen rails, screen mesh and log grates may be removed. Removed parts must be re-installable if the insert is ever removed; removing rivets or screws is acceptable.
  • Flue damper: block fully open or remove. Remove the existing chimney cap.
  • Gas line: the access hole is on the right side of the insert. In a factory-built fireplace with no gas access hole, one of 1½" or less may be drilled through the lower sides or bottom of the firebox; plug it with non-combustible insulation once the line is in. Don't route the line where it would obstruct the fan.
  • Electrical: provide power for operation; the electrical access location is in Figure 2.1.
Label the fireplace: mechanically attach the label at the bottom of the existing firebox, visible if the insert is removed. It warns that the fireplace has been converted for use with a gas fireplace insert only and cannot burn wood or solid fuels unless all original parts are replaced and the fireplace is re-approved by the Authority Having Jurisdiction.
Attach liners to the cap
Cut #816 3" flexible pipe to the measured length. Intake pipe over cap collar A; exhaust pipe (red marking) sealed onto collar B; (3) self-tapping screws each.

Each pipe must go to its correct collar on both the termination cap and the insert's vent adapter. The insert's exhaust collar is on the right side; install the cap with its exhaust collar on the right. The exhaust pipe has a red marking.

  1. Measure the total chimney length required and cut #816 (36' of 3" flexible pipe) to that length.
  2. Carefully extend the exhaust and combustion air intake pipes to the total length.
  3. Slide the intake pipe (the end without a collar) over cap collar A; secure with (3) self-tapping screws (not provided).
  4. Run a bead of sealant around the inner edge at the end of the exhaust pipe and slide it onto collar B; secure with (3) self-tapping screws (not provided) and add sealant around the joint.
Horizontal runs: maximum 24", with a 1" rise per 12" of run. Avoid tight bends that could abrade or damage the flexible pipes.
Run the vent system
Slide the vent adapter off the top of the insert. Lower both pipes down the chimney, seal and set the termination cap, and pull the pipe ends into the firebox.

1. Remove the vent adapter by sliding it back out of the channels on top of the appliance.
  2. Optional: place unfaced insulation around the first 3' of vent below the termination cap; secure with wire.
  3. Install both flexible pipes down through the chimney. With offsets, place a weighted rope around the pipe ends to guide them; never tie one rope around both pipes.
  4. Apply a liberal bead of sealant (provided) around the top of the chimney and set the cap per the vent manufacturer's manual. Optional for #816-CAP: secure with 2" self-tapping screws and anchor straps (not provided) through the pilot holes on its sides.
  5. From inside the fireplace, pull the pipes down until both the exhaust and intake are in the firebox.
  6. Optional: insulate between the pipes and the chimney to prevent heat loss.
To prevent cold air drafts, Hussong recommends insulating the 3" x 3" flexible vent pipes and chimney with unfaced insulation listed as noncombustible per ASTM E 136.
Connect & set the insert

Exhaust into the adapter collar marked 'Exhaust', intake over the intake collar, each sealed with (3) ½" self-tapping screws. Slide the insert in, pull the adapter forward with the pull rod until seated, secure with (2) ½" sheet metal screws and level.

Vent adapter

  1. Place the removed vent adapter in the fireplace opening.
  2. Exhaust pipe (red marking): bead of sealant (provided) around the pipe, slide it inside the collar marked 'Exhaust', secure with (3) ½" self-tapping screws (provided), then seal around the joint.
  3. Intake pipe: liberal bead of sealant around the intake collar, slide the pipe over it, secure with (3) ½" self-tapping screws, seal around the joint.
  4. Visually check both connections.

Place and secure

  1. Slide the insert in until the channels on top line up with the vent adapter.
  2. Put the pull rod handle through the access slot at the top and hook it through the hole in the pull rod. Push the insert in while pulling the adapter forward until seated.
  3. Secure the adapter through the slots at the top with (2) ½" sheet metal screws (components packet).
  4. Use the pull rod handle to pull the vent adapter back to its starting position, remove the handle and verify the vent connection.
  5. If needed, level the insert with the leveling bolts (components packet) threaded into the nuts underneath, 2 each side.
Gas line connection

Connect a listed ½" tee handle manual shut-off valve and flexible connector to the ½" control valve inlet, clear of the fan. Isolate the insert for supply pressure tests and leak-check every connection with soapy water.

• Manufactured for natural gas. For propane, follow the conversion kit's instructions, and convert before installing the light kit or log set.
  • Gas line by a qualified person to local codes, or ANSI Z223.1 if none. Massachusetts: a licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • Supplied: a 3/8" x 18" long flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve. Run the line in, preferably through the right gas line hole, to where the shut-off valve and flexible line connect.
  • In a minimum opening, the gas line may need to be run after the insert is placed.
  • Supply-system pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At ½ psi (3.5 kPa) or less: close its manual shut-off valve.
  • High altitude: consult the local gas distributor or the authority having jurisdiction for proper rating methods.
Leak check: check all connections, field or factory made, for leaks with soapy water.
Shroud & safety barrier
Remove both louvers and the glass, fix the shroud to the cabinet's mounting nuts with (4) truss head screws, and reinstall. Hang the safety barrier's tabs in the shroud's (4) slots.

Keep air moving: trim panels or surrounds must not seal ventilation openings in the existing fireplace, and draft relief openings must not be covered or blocked.

Shroud

  1. Lift the upper louver up and out of its mounting flanges; lift the lower louver out of the slots on its mounting bracket.
  2. Remove the glass assembly.
  3. Align the shroud's mounting holes with the mounting nuts on the sides of the insert cabinet (2 each side); secure with (4) truss head screws (provided).
  4. Reinstall everything removed.

Safety barrier

Align the tabs on the back of the barrier with the (4) slots in the shroud (2 each side), raise it slightly into the slots and let the tabs drop into place. To remove, lift up and out. The barrier must be installed; if it is damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this appliance. Barriers fit properly only when the bottom of the fireplace is level with the finished hearth. Barrier sizes are shown as drawings on p. 11.

Low mantel clearances need the CK34-LMK heat deflector on a CK34-PSF or CK34-RSF barrier: remove the (2) screws at the back of the screen front, slide the deflector under the mounting tabs and replace the screws. Its gasket must be in contact with the shroud.

Note: the arched full prairie door screen front's part number is printed as CK34A-FPDSF2 with the barrier sizes on p. 11 and as CK34-AFPDSF2 in the parts list on p. 43.
Light kit & log set
Install the (4) halogen bulbs and ember media, then set logs 1CK to 8CK of the CK34-500 set by the numbers on their bottoms. Never place logs over burner port holes.

If converting to propane, complete the conversion before installing any light kit components or the log set.

Light kit

  1. Disconnect all electrical power. Remove the safety barrier and glass frame, the logs, the burner assembly (2 screws), the side log mounting stands/refractory clips and refractory panels, the ember panel, and the burner heat shield (2 screws at the back corners).
  2. Install the (4) halogen bulbs (components packet) into the lamp bases. Never touch them with bare hands; use a soft cloth.
  3. Reinstall the ember panel. Place 2 lb. of crushed glass media (included) in the ember media cavity and scatter the klinkers on top.
  4. Reinstall the heat shield, stands/clips and panels, burner, logs, glass frame and barrier.
Note: the manual gives two ember media amounts: the light kit steps give 2 lb. (0.91 kg) of crushed glass media on p. 27; the parts list gives the ember panel crushed glass as 1.5 lb (0.68kg) on p. 43.

CK34-500 log set

  1. Position the ember panel in front of the burner.
  2. Log 1CK: align the two holes in its bottom with the two mounting pins at the back of the burner and push down to seat. Repeat for 2CK.
  3. Logs 3CK and 4CK: align the holes on their bottoms with the burner's mounting pins and push down to seat.
  4. Align 5CK with the notches in logs 1CK and 3CK; align 8CK with the notch in 4CK.
  5. Logs 6CK and 7CK: their placement is shown only in the manual's figures.
Don't place logs directly over burner port holes. Improper placement can change the flame appearance and build excessive soot on the glass.
Power up & initialize
Rocker switch OFF, (4) AA in the backup holder, (3) AAA in the remote, then connect AC power. Press SW1 ((3) beeps, amber LED) and the remote's ON/OFF within (5) seconds; the pilot lights.

1. Set the main ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF.
  2. Install (4) AA batteries (not included) in the backup battery holder on the control module, and (3) AAA batteries (components packet) in the remote's battery bay at its base.
  3. Connect the IFC module to AC power: three-prong plug into a properly grounded receptacle.
  4. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox. From here the igniter sparks repeatedly and the pilot will light if gas is supplied.
  5. Press the red SW1 button on the IFC module: (3) beeps and an amber LED mean it is ready to synchronize.
  6. Within (5) seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: (4) beeps confirm the code is accepted and the pilot ignites.
  7. Press ON/OFF again; the pilot goes out, confirming the command. The system is initialized.
  8. Set the rocker switch to ON for remote operation of the main burner and features.

Manual operation (no remote)

With the rocker switch OFF, press SW1 until (3) beeps and the amber LED, then press SW1 again within (5) seconds; the pilot lights. The rocker switch then turns the main burner on and off, and it runs on HI only.
Pressure test & flame check
Read inlet pressure at the valve's IN tap and manifold pressure at the OUT tap with a manometer; re-tighten each tap and confirm it reads no pressure. Check that flames turn yellow within 15 minutes.

1. Inlet (tap A, marked IN): with all other gas appliances in the house on, loosen the tap screw counterclockwise, attach a manometer with a ¼" I.D. hose, light pilot and burner, and confirm the reading is between minimum and maximum.
  2. Turn off burner and pilot, remove the hose and tighten the tap clockwise: snug, not over-tight. Relight and reattach the manometer to confirm the tap is sealed: no pressure.
  3. Manifold (tap B, marked OUT): light the pilot, loosen the tap, attach the manometer, light the burner and read.
  4. Turn burner and pilot off, remove the hose, tighten snug, then reattach to confirm it reads no pressure with pilot and burner on.

If inlet pressure is too high or too low, contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming gas pressure.

Flames start blue and should turn yellow during the first 15 minutes. If they don't, see the venturi settings (Section 12.2).

panels.title: Pilot will not light
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power or use battery back-up
On battery back-up → make sure the batteries are fully charged
Wiring disconnection → check every connection against the wiring schematic
Gas supply off → check shut-off valves; there may be more than one to the main line

panels.title: Pilot will not stay lit
items: No propane in tank → check and refill
Low gas pressure (bent line, too-narrow pipe, low line pressure) → plumber or gas supplier
Pilot flame not contacting the rectification sensor → pilot screw on valve: clockwise lowers, counterclockwise raises
Pilot adjustment screw not sealed → seal it; don't over-tighten

panels.title: Main burner will not light
items: ON/OFF rocker switch OFF → switch it ON
Gas off or low supply → check every shut-off; check the propane tank
Wiring fault or plugged main burner orifice → correct wiring; remove the blockage
Pilot not directed at burner, remote batteries low, or no call for heat (remote ON, thermostat OFF)

panels.title: Pilot and burner go out in operation
items: No propane in tank → check and refill
Glass assembly installed incorrectly → reinstall per Section 9.1
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris
Exhaust pipe leaking exhaust back into the firebox → find and repair

codes: Battery backup below 4V; replace the batteries
No flame after both ignition tries; verify gas on and sensor not shorted, then reset

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself. An ignition device lights the pilot automatically, so never try to light the pilot by hand.

Day to day, just press ON/OFF on the remote. The main ON/OFF rocker switch needs to be ON for the remote to run the burner.

Start-up steps from the manual

  1. Read the safety information first.
  2. Press OFF on the remote, then turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  3. Find the manual gas valve your service technician installed. Turn it clockwise to OFF.
  4. Wait five minutes to clear out any gas. Then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  5. No gas smell? Turn the valve counterclockwise to ON.
  6. Turn the electric power back on, then press ON on the remote.

If it still won't run, turn off the gas (below) and call your service technician or gas supplier.

To turn off the gas

Press OFF on the remote. Turn off the electric power too if service is planned. Then turn the manual valve clockwise to OFF.

Hands only. Turn the valve by hand, never with tools. If it won't turn, don't force it or try to fix it. Call a qualified service technician.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs the fireplace. A single beep from the fireplace confirms commands like on, off and flame changes.

  • ON/OFF: turns the fireplace on (the screen shows all active icons) or off (the screen shows only the room temperature).
  • Flame height: 6 levels. Each press of the down arrow lowers the flame one level, all the way to off. The up arrow raises it. If the system is on but the flame is off, the up arrow relights it on HI.
  • Thermostat: press the thermostat key, then set the temperature with the arrows. Press it until SMART appears and the fireplace turns the flame down as the room reaches your setting. In smart mode you can't change the flame by hand.
  • Fan: press Mode until the fan icon shows, then use the arrows (6 speeds). In thermostat mode the fan waits 5 minutes after the fire lights and keeps running about 12 minutes after it turns off. In manual mode there's no delay.
  • Light (if fitted): press Mode until the light icon shows; 6 brightness levels.
  • Key lock: press Mode and the up arrow together. A lock icon appears.
  • °F or °C: with the system off, press the thermostat key and Mode together.

sounds.title: That sound or smell is probably normal
sounds.html:
Foggy glass

When you first light the fireplace, condensation forms on the glass. This is normal in all gas fireplaces and clears after several minutes.

A paint smell

Expect a paint smell during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during this time. It helps the paint cure faster.

Ticking and creaking

The metal expands as it heats and contracts as it cools, so you may hear noises. This is normal and doesn't affect how well or how long the fireplace works.

Blue flames at first

When first lit, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn yellow. Lazy, yellow flames are what you want.

When to call: if the flames stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips and soot, the burner may need adjusting. Only a qualified service technician should do that. A smell of gas is different: follow the gas-smell steps right away.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass once a year. Wait until the fireplace is completely cool: never clean the glass, or remove it, while it's hot.

  1. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. Pull the two spring-loaded latches at the bottom of the firebox out and down. Lift the glass assembly up and off the two tabs at the top.
  4. Clean the glass with a suitable fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. To refit, set the slots on top over the tabs, lower the bottom, then pull the latches out and up to lock it.
  6. Rehang the safety screen. Don't run the fireplace without it.
Never run it with the glass removed, cracked or broken. Avoid striking or slamming the glass, and wear protective gloves to handle broken glass. Replacement glass comes only from Hussong Mfg. as a complete assembly (#701-001T), fitted by a licensed or qualified service person.
Soot on the glass? The logs may be out of place or the burner air may need adjusting. Call your service technician.

wontlight.title: If it won't light
wontlight.html:
When you press ON/OFF, the fireplace starts sparking at the pilot about 4 seconds later. It makes 2 tries of about 60 seconds each, about 35 seconds apart. If the pilot still hasn't lit, it locks out and the red LED on the control module blinks 3 times, over and over.

Reset after a lockout (any one)

  • Set the ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF, wait about 2 seconds, then set it back to ON.
  • Press ON/OFF on the remote, wait about 2 seconds, then press it again.
  • Press the down arrow until the screen shows OFF, wait about 2 seconds, then press the up arrow.

Quick checks

  • Is the gas on? There may be more than one shut-off valve between the fireplace and the main gas line.
  • On propane? Make sure the tank isn't empty.
  • Is the rocker switch ON?
  • No response at all? Replace the remote and backup batteries.
  • No call for heat? Make sure the remote is on and its thermostat operation is off.
Red LED blinks: 1 means the backup batteries are low, 2 means a pilot flame error (contact your dealer), 3 means lockout. Anything past these checks is a job for a qualified technician.

pilot.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
pilot.html:
Your fireplace can run its pilot two ways, and you choose on the remote.

IPI (spark-to-pilot)the pilot is sparked each time the fireplace turns on
CPI (continuous)the pilot stays lit, even with the burner off

A continuous pilot keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the main burner lights with less air-flow disruption.

Switch modes

  1. With the system off, press Mode until the CPI icon (a snowflake) shows.
  2. Press the up arrow for CPI, or the down arrow to go back to IPI. A single beep confirms.

When the fireplace is on, a snowflake on the screen means CPI and no snowflake means IPI. If the pilot is always on and won't go out, it's set to CPI.

Why the pilot went out on its own

  • 7-day timeout: in CPI, if the main burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns off. It's a standard safety feature. Each time the burner lights, the 7-day count starts over.
  • Safety check: within 24 hours of a continuously lit pilot, the system turns itself off for about 5 seconds to check its safety functions, then repeats your last command.

power.title: Power & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on 120V house power. Its power supply must stay live at all times and must not have a switch installed in it.

In a power outage

A backup battery pack takes over and runs the burner only. The fan and light won't work on battery power.

Backup pack (control module)(4) AA, not included
Remote(3) AAA, included

Low batteries

  • Backup pack: the fireplace gives a low double-beep when it gets an ON/OFF command, and the red LED blinks once, over and over. It won't accept more commands until you replace the batteries. It beeps once when powered after the change.
  • Remote: a battery icon appears on its screen before the power runs out. It goes away once you put in new batteries.

Battery life depends on battery quality, how many times the fireplace lights and, for the remote, how often you change the thermostat setting.

Plug it straight into a properly grounded three-prong outlet. Never cut or remove the grounding prong.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before using the fireplace, smell around it for gas, including next to the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles low.

Hot glass and children

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the safety barrier in place. If it's damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this fireplace.
  • Watch young children closely in the same room. If anyone at risk lives with you, a physical barrier such as an adjustable safety gate is recommended.

Always

  • Keep clothing, gasoline and other flammables away from the fireplace.
  • Never burn wood, coal, paper or cardboard in it.
  • Don't use it if any part has been under water. Call a qualified service technician.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year. Lots of lint from carpets or bedding can mean it needs cleaning more often.

Glassyou, yearly; technician, yearly
Fireboxtechnician, yearly
Vent systemtechnician, yearly
Burner & pilottechnician, yearly
Fantechnician, every 6 months

What the technician checks

  • Vacuums the firebox, burner system and fan. The fan's bearings are sealed and need no oil.
  • Checks the bottom latch assembly, and the glass for cracks, scratches and nicks.
  • Examines the vent system. Combustion and ventilation air must flow freely.
  • Checks gas tubes and connections for leaks, and tests the flame safety system.
  • Confirms the main burner lights within 4 seconds of the gas valve opening and the flames are steady, not lifting or floating.
Keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that can burn. Any screen or barrier removed for service must go back on before you use the fireplace.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg.'s Limited Lifetime Warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship, from the date of purchase, for the original purchaser only.

30 days · parts & laborpaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts & laborall other parts and material
Years 2 to lifetime · parts onlyfirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed to an authorized dealer only.

Making a claim

There's nothing to send in to register. Keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

Voids or isn't covered

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not installed, operated and maintained per the manual
  • Serial number or testing label removed, or any alteration or tampering
  • Submersion in water, long dampness or condensation, or water damage
  • Normal wear and tear, chimney parts, non-Hussong accessories, and how well it heats your space
This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas min / max5" WC (1.25 kPa) / 10.5" WC (2.62 kPa)
Natural gas recommended7" WC (1.74 kPa)
Propane min / max12" WC (2.99 kPa) / 13" WC (3.24 kPa)
Propane recommended12" WC (2.99 kPa) (Table 7.1)

Measure at the valve's inlet tap (A, marked IN) with all other gas appliances in the house on, using a manometer on a ¼" (6mm) I.D. hose. If the reading is too high or too low, contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming gas pressure.

Supply-system pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At ½ psi (3.5 kPa) or less, close its manual shut-off valve.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas low / high1.1" / 3.8" WC (0.27 / 0.95 kPa)
Propane low / high2.9" / 11" WC (0.72 / 2.74 kPa)

Measure at the outlet tap (B, marked OUT): light the pilot, loosen the tap screw counterclockwise, attach a manometer with a ¼ in (6mm) I.D. hose, light the burner and read. Turn burner and pilot off, tighten the tap snug (don't over-tighten), then reattach the manometer: it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on.

Gas pressure that is too high can cause lifting (ghosting) flames; check manometer settings (Table 12.4).

For a solid fuel masonry or factory-built non-combustible fireplace installed to national, provincial, state and local building codes. Keep enough access for servicing.

  • Smoke shelves, shields and baffles may be removed if attached by mechanical fasteners; remove firebrick if needed to reach the minimum opening.
  • Cutting any sheet metal parts of the existing fireplace is prohibited.
  • If the metal floor is removed, set the insert directly on the metal base of the metal fireplace.

The insert's own dimensions are shown only as a drawing (Figure 2.1, p. 9).

specVent.title: Chimney & venting
specVent.html:
Ventco-linear 3" x 3" flexible pipe

The insert must not share or be connected to a chimney flue serving any other appliance. Each pipe goes to its correct collar on the cap and the vent adapter: the exhaust collar is on the right, and the exhaust pipe has a red marking.

Approved systems

Kozy Heat #816 (one roll of 36' expandable 3" flexible pipe) with the #816-CAP round termination cap, for minimum 6" x 8" I.D. masonry or 7" I.D. Class A metal chimneys. Other approved vent manufacturers: BDM, American Metals (Amerivent), Metal Fab, Selkirk, Simpson Dura-Vent and ICC.

Co-linear to co-axial

Where a chimney no longer terminates through the roof line, an approved 4" x 6-5/8" adapter may be installed where the chimney ends. After it, the co-axial pipe needs 1" clearance to combustibles on all sides. Total co-linear plus co-axial vent: 10' minimum, 50' maximum.

Termination

Approved vent caps need 12" clearance to intersecting walls, overhangs or eaves. Two vertical terminations need 12" between them. Minimum co-axial termination height (H) above the roof, by roof pitch (Table 4.1):

specClear.title: Clearances & hearth
specClear.html:
Adjacent sidewall6" (152mm) from the appliance sides
Enclosure floor to ceiling55" (1.40m) min.
9" mantel16" (406mm) above top of appliance
6" mantel with CK34-LMK11" (279mm) above top of appliance
Maker's brochure: mantel 9" deep: 16" from top of insert (11" with Low Mantel Kit). Install to the manual.

Mantel projections can increase 1" in depth for every 1" of height, starting from the 9" mantel (or the 6" mantel with the kit). The CK34-LMK low mantel kit is only for use with safety barriers CK34-RSF and CK34-PSF.

Hearth

If combustible material is used as a hearth in front of the unit, follow one of two options:

  • Option 1: combustible flooring flush in front: install non-combustible hearth protection directly in front of the appliance, above the combustible floor, at least 7" deep, 33-1/2" long and 1/2" high.
  • Option 2: raise the appliance 1" (25mm) off the floor; combustible flooring may then be built in front.

Safety barriers install properly only with the bottom of the fireplace level with the finished hearth; allow for the hearth finish height when building a platform.

The manual's text on p. 22 prints the floor-to-ceiling clearance as 55" (1.04m); Figures 8.2 and 8.4 on p. 23 and p. 25 give 55" (1.40m).

specElec.html:
Junction box120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps
Backup battery holder(4) AA (not included)
Remote(3) AAA (included)
Light kit bulbs(4) 20W 120V halogen, 600-676
  • The AC supply must be hot at all times and must not have a switch installed in it. Shut off the household breaker before working on electrical lines.
  • Three-prong (grounding) plug: plug directly into a properly grounded three-prong receptacle; never cut or remove the grounding prong. Ground per local codes, or the National Electrical Code ANSI/NFPA 70 or the Canadian Electrical Code CSA C22.1.
  • The IFC module runs on 120V and/or batteries. Battery back-up operates the burner only; fan and light don't work on battery power.
  • Electrical access location: Figure 2.1. Wiring schematic: Figure 10.1 (a diagram).
  • Don't use the appliance if any part has been under water; a qualified service technician must inspect it and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that was under water.

specVenturi.title: Burner venturi & flame
specVenturi.html:
Natural gas1/8" (3mm) open
Propane5/8" (16mm) open

Factory set. Venturi adjustment must be done by a qualified service technician. Flames start blue and should turn yellow over the first 15 minutes; lazy, yellow flames need no adjustment. If they stay blue, or go dark orange with black tips (sooting), the air shutter may need adjusting. Closing the shutter gives a yellow flame but may soot the glass; opening it gives a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner.

Table 12.4

Dark, orange flame, black tipsventuri closed too far: open slightly
Short, blue flamesventuri open too far: close slightly
Lifting (ghosting) flamesgas pressure too high (check manometer) or venturi closed too far (open slightly)
Note: the manual gives both directions for adjusting blue, lifting flames. On p. 38 the text says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner, and Table 12.4 says to close the venturi slightly for short, blue flames. But Table 12.4 also lists "venturi closed too far" as a cause of lifting flames, and the troubleshooting chart on p. 40 says to open the air shutter slightly when the flame burns blue and lifts off the burner.

Adjusting

  1. Soot on the glass? Check log positioning first; logs must not block burner ports.
  2. Let the fireplace cool. Remove the safety barrier and glass frame, the log set and the burner assembly.
  3. Loosen the screws on the venturi, adjust, re-tighten, and reinstall everything.
  4. Slight adjustments give dramatic results. Burn at least 15 minutes and let it cool before adjusting further.

Soot on the glass can also come from incorrect vent cap installation or a blocked vent cap.

review.notes: Single source: CSK-34-L Installation & Operation Manual R.11 (Sept 2022); pages 2, 4, 6 and 45 are blank. No French-only or font-scrambled text. Ignition: Proflame 2 IFC with SIT IPI valve; spark-to-pilot (IPI) by default with a selectable continuous pilot (CPI) and 7-day CPI timeout; remote-operated, with a rocker-switch manual mode (HI only). Not transcribed (figure-only): appliance dimensions (Figure 2.1, p. 9: the numbers 23", 33 3/8" and 16" appear but the text doesn't say which is height, width or depth, so catalog height/width/depth can't be confirmed), safety barrier sizes (p. 11), placement of logs 6CK and 7CK (p. 28), wiring schematic (p. 30). The manual gives no efficiency rating or viewing area, so catalog efficiency (75.0/77.0 AFUE) and view_area can't be checked; the parts list gives the glass as 31-1/2" x 19-5/8". Table 7.1 (p. 21) prints 'recommended' under the propane minimum (12" WC) with no value of its own; the guide gives only the 12"-13" WC propane range and the 7" WC natural gas recommendation. Section 11.9.5 'Turn OFF the appliance' (p. 35) repeats the turn-ON wording ('with the system in the OFF position... to turn ON'); the result text says only room temperature shows and the burner turns off, so the guide describes ON/OFF as toggling. p. 11 points to 'section 8.3 Safety Barrier Installation on page 25'; it is Section 8.4 on p. 26. Troubleshooting (p. 39): the line 'Ensure batteries are fully charged if using battery back-up' sits between two causes, so the guide lists it as its own item. The fan is listed as a field-assembled part (Table 2.1) but the remote section calls fan speed control 'optional'; the catalog says the fan kit is included. Not flagged as a mismatch. Massachusetts sidewall-vent CO detector and signage rules (Section 1.3, p. 7) are left out because they cover sidewall horizontally vented equipment; this insert vents up the chimney. Leak testing with soapy water comes from the control board section caution (p. 29); the gas line section (p. 21) doesn't describe a leak test.
